comparisons.peer_summary: Client operating income improved to an $897 million profit in 2024 from a $46 million operating loss in 2023, primarily due to higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD attribute their respective segment financial improvements in fiscal 2024 primarily to higher revenue. QCOM’s QCT segment revenue growth was driven by higher handset chipset shipments ($2.8 billion) and automotive demand, which led to an increase in EBT margin. Similarly, AMD’s Client segment operating income improved from a loss to a profit primarily due to higher revenue, although AMD explicitly notes this was partially offset by higher operating expenses, whereas QCOM highlights the margin expansion directly from the revenue scale.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze segment operating/income performance drivers relative to the prior year. QCOM attributes its QCT EBT margin increase to higher revenues. AMD’s Data Center segment similarly saw operating income rise to $3.5 billion from $1.3 billion, primarily driven by higher revenue (sales of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs), though AMD also notes the offset of higher R&D investment, a specific cost factor not cited as a margin dragger in the QCOM excerpt.

comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail the composition of revenue changes for a client-facing computing segment. QCOM’s QCT handset revenue increased due to higher chipset shipments, partially offset by lower revenue per chipset (unfavorable mix). INTC’s CCG revenue increased 4% due to higher notebook volume, partially offset by lower desktop revenue and exit of legacy businesses. Both companies are analyzing client device revenue mix and volume shifts against prior year performance.

comparisons.peer_summary: EBU operating income decreased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to declines in average selling prices, partially offset by higher bit shipments and cost reductions.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the impact of pricing and volume on financial results, but with opposite directions. QCOM’s QCT handset revenue included $533 million in lower revenues per chipset due to unfavorable mix/pricing, yet overall revenue increased due to volume. In contrast, MU’s EBU operating income decreased primarily due to declines in average selling prices (ASP), although it was offset by higher bit shipments, similar to the volume offset seen at QCOM.
